text:
anya: Heads-up — saw a weird pattern this morning: a bunch of streams that were idle-closed by the server and then immediately re-opened. Console shows two separate sessions and cost doubled for a handful of customers.

sam: Yup, I caught the logs. Server FIN at 08:12:17, client reconnect at 08:12:17.2 but no resume token on the re-open, so runtime treats it as a fresh session.

anya: Here's the snippet from the edge-proxy logs (redacted):
```
[08:12:17.000] -> SERVER: idle-close reason=idle_timeout session_id=abc123
[08:12:17.203] <- CLIENT: ws-handshake session_hint=abc123
headers: { "sec-websocket-protocol": "redwood-stream", "x-client-id":"svc-12" }
# note: no x-resume-token header
```

marta: Console is attributing metrics per session_id but the re-open gets a new session_id because resume failed. So traces look like two independent streams. UX-wise it shows two billed rows side-by-side.

kevin: If it's actually the same logical work, double billing is bad. But we need to be careful about edge cases — ignoring opens might be abused.

anya: Agreed. I think root cause is server-initiated idle close + client reconnect path that doesn't attempt resume if the proxy stripped the resume header. We should verify whether the proxy is dropping `x-resume-token` on 101 responses.

sam: On the edge side, we only forward resume if it's present in the initial handshake. There's a small race where the token cookie can be evicted from the client store after close. But in these logs the client never sent it on reconnect. Could be client lib fallback.

marta: For the console, we could group temporally adjacent session opens as one logical session when certain heuristics match (same user id, same client ip, time delta < 5s). Then show a collapsed row and a badge like `transient_reconnect`.

kevin: That helps UX, but billing-wise we need a defensible heuristic. Proposal: don't bill the second session if (1) token_count < 50 tokens, (2) delta < 5s, (3) same client fingerprint, and (4) we recorded a `resume_failed` event in telemetry. Otherwise bill normally.

anya: That seems reasonable. Also emits `resume_failed` in telemetry so product + billing can audit. Right now we only log `stream_close` and `stream_open` events — no explicit `resume_failed` when a reconnect lacks token.

sam: Implementation notes: runtime should emit `resume_attempt` | `resume_succeeded` | `resume_failed`. Edge-proxy should preserve `x-resume-token` on websocket handshake; add a debug flag to log header presence for a short window.

marta: I'll sketch the UI: grouping toggle, badge, and a link to raw events that expands to show both opens. Default: collapsed grouping to reduce noise. We'll still allow uncollapse for audit.

kevin: Add a metric in billing pipeline to count grouped_reconnects and grouped_token_ignores so we can measure abuse. Also add a rejection rate threshold before we relax billing.

anya: Also a short-term mitigation: increase server idle-close threshold from 60s -> 90s for affected tenants to reduce occurrences while we fix the header handling.

deploy-bot: Deployment planned: edge-proxy header-preserve fix -> canary Thu 09:00 UTC, rollout Fri 03:00 UTC. console change -> mock -> canary Mon 07:00 UTC.

sam: I'll own the runtime telemetry events. Will add a small trace tag `resume_hint=<missing|present>` so downstream can correlate.

marta: Filing a tiny UX ticket and the console mock link: https://canv.as/s/console-reconnect-mock (internal). Putting PR checklist in the ticket.

kevin: OK. For billing policy, I'll draft the formal heuristic and share with legal. If we see >0.5% abuse in 7d we revert.

anya: Thanks everyone. Action items: sam -> telemetry + runtime events; marta -> console grouping mock + PR; sam/anya -> edge-proxy header audit + canary; kevin -> draft billing heuristic + alerts. Follow-up sync in #eng-platform tomorrow.

prod-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-447 — "transient reconnect doubling sessions" (severity: low)
